scope: host-side three-path parity; not a final evaluation, not an accuracy/board/navigation claim

data.final_pool_policy: read-only sample; no metrics run, no label/threshold change, final never rerun

paths.pt_square: ultralytics .pt predict on the shared 640x640 canvas, decode model->source
paths.onnx_native_square: ultralytics .onnx predict on the same canvas
paths.raw_ort_square: onnxruntime + numpy NMS (iou 0.7, max_det 300) + eval-tool decode

raw_numeric_parity.note: the 2026-11-04 smoke-checkpoint claim was a 1.22e-4 absolute max on an untrained graph; on the trained checkpoint the absolute max is dominated by the coordinate channels (~1e-4 relative to 640), which is why the pass criterion is relative.  The decision-level effect is measured by the three-path comparisons.

legacy_4_67px_explanation.reading: legacy .pt and .onnx ultralytics predictors build different letterboxes (auto/rect vs square); the shared-canvas paths remove that difference, so a large legacy keypoint delta is a preprocessing-mode artefact, not a graph/export error

decision_flip_answer.reading: with one shared preprocessing mode the three paths must agree on every decision; the legacy mismatch is the only place where the old 4.67 px class of difference can flip a pass/fail decision, and the flip count is reported above

limitations: synthetic aspect/edge/multi-candidate variants have no GT, so their comparison is observation-level only
near-threshold selection uses the raw ORT top score on the sampled frames, not a population estimate
the exploratory final pool was sampled read-only after its single one-shot evaluation; no new final metrics were produced
RKNN/board, real camera, accuracy certification remain out of scope (UNKNOWN)
